We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=1-2{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(1-2{x}^{2})(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(-4x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{4x}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})-\int (\frac{{e}^{4x}}{4})(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{1}{4}\int {e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{4x}}{4}-\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+(\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C) \\  & =\frac{(1-2{x}^{2}){e}^{4x}}{4}+\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(4x-1)+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{16}(-8{x}^{2}+4x+3)+C.\end{aligned}
$$
